title: Whole question reduces to specific vs accidental difference — small once living alone saves
source_text: L. Itaque quamvis Doctores illi dicant fidem justificantem specie non differre a fide dogmatica, quam historicam Reformati appellant, nihilominus cum Reformatis agnoscunt solam fidem vivam atque efficacem hominem, ut jam dictum est, actu servare & justificare, minime vero istud convenire fidei mortuae atque otiosae. Ac juxta eorum hypotheses ista simul consistunt solam fidem vivam justificare & tamen fidem justificantem a fide mortua & mere dogmatica non esse specie diversam, quia, scilicet, supponunt fidem vivam tantum accidentaliter a fide mortua differre. Ac proinde huc redit tota quaestio, An scilicet fides viva & per charitatem operans a fide mortua specie, vel genere differat, quod tenent Reformati: An vero inter utramque sit accidentale tantum quoddam discrimen; quod communiter docet Schola Romana? Quae quidem quaestio mere Scholastica & Philosophica est, nec admodum magni momenti, dum constet salutem atque justitiam non fidei mortuae, sed vivae tribuendam esse, quod utrinque in confesso est.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore although those Doctors say justifying faith does not differ specifically from dogmatic faith, which the Reformed call historic, nevertheless with the Reformed they acknowledge that only living and efficacious faith actually saves and justifies a person, as already said, and that this by no means belongs to dead and idle faith. And according to their hypotheses these stand together: that only living faith justifies, and yet justifying faith is not specifically diverse from dead and merely dogmatic faith, because they suppose living faith differs from dead only accidentally. And so the whole question returns to this: whether living faith working through charity differs from dead faith in species or genus, which the Reformed hold; or whether between the two there is only a certain accidental difference, which the Roman school commonly teaches. Which question is merely scholastic and philosophical, and not of very great moment, so long as it is settled that salvation and justice are to be attributed not to dead faith but to living, which is confessed on both sides.
pass_b_english: Rome can say justifying faith is not specifically other than dogmatic/historic yet still join Reformed in granting only living efficacious faith actually saves.
The dispute shrinks to specific/generic vs merely accidental difference — scholastic and small once both sides attribute salvation to living not dead faith.

choices.why: Irénic reduction once living-alone-saves is shared.
